document.abstract: A fine-grain AgBr emulsion, prepared with an inert gelatin, shows no reciprocity failure at very short exposures if the chemical aging has been effected in the absence of S=-unstable ions. In an emulsion with coarse grains (which has therefore undergone the physical aging) there is considerable reciprocity failure. This is due to the fact that the surface-to-volume ratio in these emulsions is smaller than in those with fine grain, so that a gelatin which is inert for the latter is not so for an emulsion with coarse grains. If AgI is added to a fine-grain AgBr emulsion which showed no reciprocity failure, there appears a considerable reciprocity failure at very short exposures.
